beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Substrate Cycle asks who controls reality after ordinary scarcity changes shape.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its two science-fiction investigations connect abundance with power over the systems beneath it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One begins with a suspicious death before a city's scheduled flooding.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A collective decision becomes difficult because its costs belong to particular lives.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The other follows a missing infant through a household's disputed care records.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The mysteries make institutional rules matter to particular people before demanding larger judgments.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Dordrecht's gate has a scheduled opening, and residents gather to witness it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Some support the restoration while others face the loss it will bring.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The assisting intelligence can display consequences without making those consequences belong equally to everyone.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The scene gives collective choice a physical place and a moment of irreversibility.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Material abundance does not remove the need to decide whose losses are acceptable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The first story develops that tension through a changed economy and shared infrastructure.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The second story follows an infant with thirty-seven legal parents.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Her disappearance exposes disputes over which adults caused which parts of her care.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One held her, another prepared milk, and another settled an older child.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The law makes care visible, yet recognition can become political power.
